전도서-10-1.title: 전도서 10장 1절 역사문법적 주해
전도서-10-1.exegesis: 18. one sinner, &c.-- ( Jos 7:1 , 11, 12 ). Though wisdom excels folly ( Ec 9:16 ; 7:19 ), yet a "little folly (equivalent to sin) can destroy much good," both in himself ( Ec 10:1 ; Jas 2:10 ) and in others. "Wisdom" must, from the antithesis to "sinner," mean religion. Thus typically, the "little city" may be applied to the Church ( Lu 12:32 ; He 12:22 ); the great king to Satan ( Joh 12:31 ); the despised poor wise man, Jesus Christ ( Is 53:2 , 3 ; Mr 6:3 ; 2Co 8:9 ; Ep 1:7 , 8 ; Col 2:3 ).

전도서-10-2.title: 전도서 10장 2절 역사문법적 주해
전도서-10-2.exegesis: CHAPTER 10 Ec 10:1-20 . 1. Following up Ec 9:18 . him that is in reputation-- for example, David ( 2Sa 12:14 ); Solomon ( 1Ki 11:1-43 ); Jehoshaphat (2Ch 18:1-34; 19:2); Josiah ( 2Ch 35:22 ). The more delicate the perfume, the more easily spoiled is the ointment. Common oil is not so liable to injury. So the higher a man's religious character is, the more hurt is caused by a sinful folly in him. Bad savor is endurable in oil, but not in what professes to be, and is compounded by the perfumer ("apothecary") for, fragrance. "Flies" answer to "a little folly" (sin), appropriately, being small ( 1Co 5:6 ); also, "Beelzebub" means prince of flies. "Ointment" answers to "reputation" ( Ec 7:1 ; Ge 34:30 ). The verbs are singular, the noun plural, implying that each of the flies causes the stinking savor.

전도서-10-3.title: 전도서 10장 3절 역사문법적 주해
전도서-10-3.exegesis: 2. ( Ec 2:14 ). right-- The right hand is more expert than the left. The godly wise is more on his guard than the foolish sinner, though at times he slip. Better a diamond with a flaw, than a pebble without one.

전도서-10-4.title: 전도서 10장 4절 역사문법적 주해
전도서-10-4.exegesis: 3. by the way-- in his ordinary course; in his simplest acts ( Pr 6:12-14 ). That he "saith," virtually, "that he" himself, &c. [Septuagint]. But Vulgate, "He thinks that every one (else whom he meets) is a fool."

전도서-10-5.title: 전도서 10장 5절 역사문법적 주해
전도서-10-5.exegesis: 4. spirit-- anger. yielding pacifieth-- ( Pr 15:1 ). This explains "leave not thy place"; do not in a resisting spirit withdraw from thy post of duty ( Ec 8:3 ).
전도서-10-5.theologicalNote: 4. spirit-- anger. yielding pacifieth-- ( Pr 15:1 ). This explains "leave not thy place"; do not in a resisting spirit withdraw from thy post of duty ( Ec 8:3 ).

전도서-10-6.title: 전도서 10장 6절 역사문법적 주해
전도서-10-6.exegesis: 5. as-- rather, "by reason of an error" [Maurer and Holden].
전도서-10-6.theologicalNote: 5. as-- rather, "by reason of an error" [Maurer and Holden].

전도서-10-7.title: 전도서 10장 7절 역사문법적 주해
전도서-10-7.exegesis: 6. rich-- not in mere wealth, but in wisdom, as the antithesis to "folly" (for "foolish men") shows. So Hebrew, rich, equivalent to "liberal," in a good sense ( Is 32:5 ). Mordecai and Haman ( Es 3:1 , 2; 6:6-11 ).

전도서-10-8.title: 전도서 10장 8절 역사문법적 주해
전도서-10-8.exegesis: 7. servants upon horses-- the worthless exalted to dignity ( Jr 17:25 ); and vice versa ( 2Sa 15:30 ).
전도서-10-8.theologicalNote: 7. servants upon horses-- the worthless exalted to dignity ( Jr 17:25 ); and vice versa ( 2Sa 15:30 ).

전도서-10-9.title: 전도서 10장 9절 역사문법적 주해
전도서-10-9.exegesis: 8. The fatal results to kings of such an unwise policy; the wrong done to others recoils on themselves ( Ec 8:9 ); they fall into the pit which they dug for others ( Es 7:10 ; Psa 7:15 ; Pr 26:27 ). Breaking through the wise fences of their throne, they suffer unexpectedly themselves; as when one is stung by a serpent lurking in the stones of his neighbor's garden wall ( Psa 80:12 ), which he maliciously pulls down ( Am 5:19 ).

전도서-10-10.title: 전도서 10장 10절 역사문법적 주해
전도서-10-10.exegesis: 9. removeth stones-- namely, of an ancient building [Weiss]. His neighbor's landmarks [Holden]. Cuts out from the quarry [Maurer]. endangered-- by the splinters, or by the head of the hatchet, flying back on himself. Pithy aphorisms are common in the East. The sense is: Violations of true wisdom recoil on the perpetrators.

전도서-10-11.title: 전도서 10장 11절 역사문법적 주해
전도서-10-11.exegesis: 10. iron ... blunt-- in "cleaving wood" ( Ec 10:9 ), answering to the "fool set in dignity" ( Ec 10:6 ), who wants sharpness. More force has then to be used in both cases; but "force" without judgment "endangers" one's self. Translate, "If one hath blunted his iron" [Maurer]. The preference of rash to judicious counsellors, which entailed the pushing of matters by force, proved to be the "hurt" of Rehoboam ( 1Ki 12:1-33 ). wisdom is profitable to direct-- to a prosperous issue. Instead of forcing matters by main "strength" to one's own hurt ( Ec 9:16 , 18 ).

전도서-10-12.title: 전도서 10장 12절 역사문법적 주해
전도서-10-12.exegesis: 11. A "serpent will bite" if "enchantment" is not used; "and a babbling calumniator is no better." Therefore, as one may escape a serpent by charms ( Psa 58:4 , 5 ), so one may escape the sting of a calumniator by discretion ( Ec 10:12 ), [Holden]. Thus, "without enchantment" answers to "not whet the edge" ( Ec 10:10 ), both expressing, figuratively, want of judgment. Maurer translates, "There is no gain to the enchanter" (Margin, "master of the tongue") from his enchantments, because the serpent bites before he can use them; hence the need of continual caution. Ec 10:8-10 , caution in acting; Ec 10:11 and following verses, caution in speaking.

전도서-10-13.title: 전도서 10장 13절 역사문법적 주해
전도서-10-13.exegesis: 12. gracious-- Thereby he takes precaution against sudden injury ( Ec 10:11 ). swallow up himself-- ( Pr 10:8 , 14, 21 , 32 ; 12:13 ; 15:2 ; 22:11 ).
전도서-10-13.theologicalNote: 12. gracious-- Thereby he takes precaution against sudden injury ( Ec 10:11 ). swallow up himself-- ( Pr 10:8 , 14, 21 , 32 ; 12:13 ; 15:2 ; 22:11 ).

전도서-10-14.title: 전도서 10장 14절 역사문법적 주해
전도서-10-14.exegesis: 13. Illustrating the folly and injuriousness of the fool's words; last clause of Ec 10:12 .
전도서-10-14.theologicalNote: 13. Illustrating the folly and injuriousness of the fool's words; last clause of Ec 10:12 .

전도서-10-15.title: 전도서 10장 15절 역사문법적 주해
전도서-10-15.exegesis: 14. full of words-- ( Ec 5:2 ). a man cannot tell what shall be-- ( Ec 3:22 ; 6:12 ; 8:7 ; 11:2 ; Pr 27:1 ). If man, universally (including the wise man), cannot foresee the future, much less can the fool; his "many words" are therefore futile.

전도서-10-16.title: 전도서 10장 16절 역사문법적 주해
전도서-10-16.exegesis: 15. labour ... wearieth-- ( Is 55:2 ; Ha 2:13 ). knoweth not how to go to the city-- proverb for ignorance of the most ordinary matters ( Ec 10:3 ); spiritually, the heavenly city ( Psa 107:7 ; Mt 7:13 , 14 ). Maurer connects Ec 10:15 with the following verses. The labor (vexation) caused by the foolish (injurious princes, Ec 10:4-7 ) harasses him who "knows not how to go to the city," to ingratiate himself with them there. English Version is simpler.

전도서-10-17.title: 전도서 10장 17절 역사문법적 주해
전도서-10-17.exegesis: 16. a child-- given to pleasures; behaves with childish levity. Not in years; for a nation may be happy under a young prince, as Josiah. eat in the morning-- the usual time for dispensing justice in the East ( Jr 21:12 ); here, given to feasting ( Is 5:11 ; Ac 2:15 ).

전도서-10-18.title: 전도서 10장 18절 역사문법적 주해
전도서-10-18.exegesis: 17. son of nobles-- not merely in blood, but in virtue, the true nobility ( So 7:1 ; Is 32:5 , 8 ). in due season-- ( Ec 3:1 ), not until duty has first been attended to. for strength-- to refresh the body, not for revelry (included in "drunkenness").

전도서-10-19.title: 전도서 10장 19절 역사문법적 주해
전도서-10-19.exegesis: 18. building-- literally, "the joining of the rafters," namely, the kingdom ( Ec 10:16 ; Is 3:6 ; Am 9:11 ). hands-- ( Ec 4:5 ; Pr 6:10 ). droppeth-- By neglecting to repair the roof in time, the rain gets through.

전도서-10-20.title: 전도서 10장 20절 역사문법적 주해
전도서-10-20.exegesis: 19. Referring to Ec 10:18 . Instead of repairing the breaches in the commonwealth (equivalent to "building"), the princes "make a feast for laughter ( Ec 10:16 ), and wine maketh their life glad ( Psa 104:15 ), and (but) money supplieth (answereth their wishes by supplying) all things," that is, they take bribes to support their extravagance; and hence arise the wrongs that are perpetrated ( Ec 10:5 , 6 ; 3:16 ; Is 1:23 ; 5:23). Maurer takes "all things" of the wrongs to which princes are instigated by "money"; for example, the heavy taxes, which were the occasion of Rehoboam losing ten tribes ( 1Ki 12:4 , &c.).
